uncited: This is the second phase of the iHOS method.
It takes the surface-tangent quads generated by the object space sampling and rasterizes them in image space.
Fragments from this rasterization serve as starting points for ray casting.
Directional Newton-Raphson is applied along the ray direction to refine the isosurface representation.
It is chosen when high-quality, pixel-accurate rendering is required after the initial coarse sampling.
*   **Time Complexity**: The method performs independent computations for each seed and fragment.
*   **Memory Complexity**: Low, as no neighborhood information is needed.
*   **Strengths**: The gradient integration step significantly improves the robustness of Newton-Raphson convergence by ensuring starting points are close to the isosurface.
*   **Limitations**: Holes in the isosurface can occur due to insufficient iteration counts, high curvature, or insufficient quad sizes.
It is part of a GPU-based approach for interactive rendering of isosurfaces defined by high-order multivariate polynomials.
